title: Earnings Implications of Fair Value Accounting Practices in the Oil and Gas Industry: Empirical Evidence from Nigeria
affiliations: Institute of Management and Technology (IMT), Enugu

detail.title: Earnings Implications of Fair Value Accounting Practices in the Oil and Gas Industry: Empirical Evidence from Nigeria

declarations.declarationOfInterest: no personal or financial relationship with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced the study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is based entirely on secondary data obtained from publicly available and credible sources, including annual report of MRS Oil Nigeria Plc 2015-2024. No human participants or personally identifiable information were involved in the research. As such, ethical approval and informed consent were not required. The research has adhered to all standard ethical guidelines for secondary data analysis, including proper citation, data integrity, and compliance with relevant copyright and data usage policies.

keywords: Trade and Other Payables and Impairment Loss on Financial Assets and Earnings per Share

detail.abstract: The oil and gas industry's financial reporting regulations have been drastically altered by the implementation of fair value accounting under IFRS, generating questions regarding possible impacts on business profitability and performance evaluation. The study assessed the total effects of trade and other receivables, deferred tax liabilities, trade and other payables, and impairment loss on financial assets on earnings per share of Nigerian oil and gas businesses after controlling for firm size and leverage.MRS Oil Nigeria Plc's published financial statements provided secondary data for the years 2015-2024, and an ex post facto research design was used. The established hypotheses were examined using the Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) multiple regression technique with the aid of e-views 13. To support the interpretation of the results, SWOT and PESTEL analyses were used. The regression results demonstrated that trade and other receivables, deferred tax liabilities, trade and other payables, and impairment loss on financial assets had no statistically significant impact on earnings per share during the period under review because their respective p-values (0.6194, 0.7812, 0.4186, and 0.8721) exceeded 5% significance level. The model's overall F-statistic probability value of 0.3123 indicated that it was statistically insignificant. The study comes to the conclusion that fair value accounting techniques are not very good at predicting earnings performance of Nigerian oil and gas companies. In order to improve earnings performance, the study recommends management to prioritize cost reduction, revenue optimization, and operational efficiency.

title: Manual on Training and Mentoring Real Estate Agents

detail.title: Manual on Training and Mentoring Real Estate Agents
detail.abstract:
Today's real estate market requires agents to be highly professional and efficient. Clients expect competent support for transactions, and competition between agencies is growing. In such conditions, there is a growing demand for competent realtors who are able to learn quickly and deliver results. However, the industry has traditionally faced high staff turnover. According to the National Association of Realtors, up to 75% of new agents leave the profession within the first year, and about 87% within five years. The main reasons are a lack of practical experience, insufficient support, and the formal nature of training at the beginning of a career. Therefore, agency managers are faced with the urgent task of preparing newcomers as best as possible to increase their chances of success and provide the agency with qualified personnel.

This manual clearly presents the unique approach of Maksym Herasimov to training and mentoring real estate agents. This approach combines practical field training from day one with an analytical approach to progress assessment (CRM analytics). This combined model has already proven to be highly effective in meeting the demand for professional agents.

title: Data Element Governance and Strategic Disclosure of Corporate Digital Information

detail.title: Data Element Governance and Strategic Disclosure of Corporate Digital Information

keywords: National-level Big Data Comprehensive Pilot Zone
Digital Transformation with More Talk Than Action

detail.abstract: Digital transformation is a core strategy for high-quality corporate development. However, strategic disclosure characterized by "talking the talk but not walking the walk" distorts resource allocation and hinders the deep integration of the digital economy with the real economy. This study employs the establishment of national-level big data comprehensive pilot zones as a quasi-natural experiment. Using matched data from listed companies and prefecture-level cities from 2010 to 2021, this study empirically examines the policy's effect on curbing the "talking the talk but not walking the walk" behavior in corporate digital transformation and its underlying mechanisms. Findings reveal that the establishment of big data pilot zones significantly reduces the gap between corporate digital transformation rhetoric and actual actions. Mechanism tests indicate that enhanced government-enterprise information sharing efficiency, reduced bank-enterprise information asymmetry, and improved transparency between enterprises and investors constitute the core pathways through which the policy exerts its governance effects. Further analysis shows that policy effects are more pronounced in enterprises with lower management myopia and higher analyst attention, and are more significant in regions with stronger digital economic foundations. From a corporate lifecycle perspective, the policy effectively restrains start-up and mature firms while having no significant impact on declining enterprises. Moreover, the effectiveness of bank-firm information exchange mechanisms is subject to boundary conditions: the policy's restraining effect only becomes pronounced when a firm's profitability, debt repayment capacity, and economic uncertainty align with banks' lending benchmarks. This study provides empirical evidence and policy insights for addressing pseudo-digital transformation challenges through data element governance and refining institutional mechanisms for digital economic development.

title: Mean-Field Price Formation on Trees with a Network of Relative Performance Concerns
affiliations: University of Tokyo - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: Mean-Field Price Formation on Trees with a Network of Relative Performance Concerns

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There is no competing interests to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-pro fit sectors.

detail.abstract: Financial firms and institutional investors are routinely evaluated based on their performance relative to their peers. These relative performance concerns significantly influence risk-taking behavior and market dynamics. While the literature studying Nash equilibrium under such relative performance competitions is extensive, its effect on asset price formation remains largely unexplored. This paper investigates mean-field equilibrium price formation of a single risky stock in a discrete-time market where agents exhibit exponential utility and relative performance concerns. Unlike existing literature that typically treats asset prices as exogenous, we impose a market-clearing condition to determine the price dynamics endogenously within a relative performance equilibrium. Using a binomial tree framework, we establish the existence and uniqueness of the market-clearing mean-field equilibrium in both single-and multi-population settings. Finally, we provide illustrative numerical examples demonstrating the equilibrium price distributions and agents' optimal position sizes.

title: City Formation by Dual Migration of Firms and Workers

detail.title: City Formation by Dual Migration of Firms and Workers
detail.abstract: This paper presents a mathematical model of city formation by the migration of firms and workers. The Core-Periphery model in the new economic geography, which considers the single migration of workers driven by real wage inequality among regions, is extended to incorporate the migration of firms driven by real profit inequality among regions. In this dual-migration model, the behavior of solutions is qualitatively similar to that of single-migration models. That is, 1) spatially homogeneous population distributions become destabilized and eventually form several cities where both firms and workers agglomerate; 2) the number of cities decreases as transport costs decrease. These results provide a more general theoretical justification for the use of single migration models.

title: Can LLMs "Understand" Factors? A Semantically-Enhanced Asset Pricing Model
affiliations: Wuhan University and City University of Hong Kong (CityU) - Department of Economics and Finance

detail.title: Can LLMs "Understand" Factors? A Semantically-Enhanced Asset Pricing Model
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for asset pricing that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to integrate a factor's numerical value with its semantic information. We address the limitation of existing models, which rely solely on factor values and ignore the rich economic context embedded in their textual definitions. Our method, the Semantically-Enhanced Factor Adapter (SEF-Adapter), uses a pre-trained LLM to encode factor definitions into a semantic representation, which is then fused with the factor's numerical value. Extensive experiments on the US and China stock markets demonstrate that this combination of semantic and value information significantly improves return predictability over traditional value-only models.

title: Rules and Discretion(s) in Prudential Regulation and Supervision: Evidence from EU Banks in the Run-Up to the Financial Crisis
affiliations: European Central Bank (ECB) and KU Leuven, Department Accounting, Finance and Insurance

detail.title: Rules and Discretion(s) in Prudential Regulation and Supervision: Evidence from EU Banks in the Run-Up to the Financial Crisis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The views presented in this paper are those of the authors and should not be attributed to the European Central Bank or the Eurosystem.
declarations.funderStatement: Scopelliti acknowledges financial support from Internal Funds KU Leuven (STG/21/048).

detail.abstract: Prior to the global financial crisis, prudential regulation in the EU was implemented non-uniformly across countries, as options and discretions allowed national authorities to apply a more favorable regulatory treatment. We construct country indicators of regulatory flexibility (for all banks in a country) and supervisory discretion (on a case-by-case basis). Overall, we find that banks in countries with a more lenient prudential regime were more likely to require public support during the crisis, also when controlling for bank size. Supervisory discretion was more detrimental for the stability of large banks, while regulatory flexibility increased distress probability more for medium and small banks. We provide evidence that a laxer prudential framework can increase the ex-post probability of bank distress in crisis times by enhancing bank risk-taking. The effects work through specific balance sheet channels. Banks in more flexible regulatory environments had a higher share of non-interest income and larger credit provision; banks subject to higher supervisory discretion held more liquid assets, albeit with larger sovereign exposures.

title: Formal Foundations of Multilevel Game Theory

detail.title: Formal Foundations of Multilevel Game Theory

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest. No financial relationships or competing interests influenced this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study analyzed publicly available legal documents and constitutional provisions; no human subjects were involved.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The author conducted this work independently.

detail.abstract:
Classical game theory assumes all players share the same cognitive architecture. This assumption fails in modern strategic environments where corporations (cost optimizers), algorithms (pattern matchers), and humans (social reasoners) interact simultaneously.

I extend game-theoretic foundations to accommodate heterogeneous intentionality. The framework introduces Asymmetric Intentionality Equilibrium (AIE), which exists under standard conditions and reduces to Nash Equilibrium when players share intentionality levels. When they diverge, AIE predicts systematic exploitation of higher-intentionality players by lower-intentionality entities.

The Dennett-Nash Gap quantifies this advantage. Preliminary evidence from corporate enforcement data supports the framework: public corporations show 8x higher recidivism than private firms, and penalties function as "parking tickets" rather than deterrents. These patterns suggest that legal institutions designed for shame-susceptible humans fail when applied to optimization-driven entities.

The framework has implications for corporate liability, AI governance, and contract design.
